feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated. The best raced design so far is iteration 1 (score 383.755). It finished 19 of 20 oval trials at a mean of 1.88 s. It went off_track on the s-bend (progress 0.39) and slalom (progress 0.17), with max_error about 0.062 to 0.064 m, about one line-loss event per run, and steering_oscillation about 0.21 on every track. This candidate changes three controller fields and leaves geometry fixed, so any change in result can be attributed to the controller. kp rises from 1.2 to 1.4 to address the line loss near the 0.06 m limit. kd rises from 0.3 to 0.4 to damp the jitter, which is above the 0.15 level. base_speed drops from 1.2 to 1.0 to give the robot more time to correct on the tight bends. The main risk is that the wider sensor spread (set in iteration 1) may be what raised oscillation from about 0.11 in iteration 0 to about 0.21, so kp and kd changes alone may not bring oscillation down. The lower base_speed also costs completion time on the oval. Approve it: it is a targeted, single-step change from the best design, there are enough runs left for a race, and the telemetry will sharpen the next critique. After the race, read the result as follows. If the s-bend and slalom still end off_track with low steering_oscillation (below about 0.15), raise kp toward 1.6. If oscillation stays above 0.15 while the robot stays on the line, lower kp or raise kd toward 0.5. If the oval finishes but completion_time is above 3 s, raise base_speed toward 1.3. Do not change geometry until the controller is tuned on the widened sensor spread.
requested_changes: If the s-bend and slalom still end off_track with steering_oscillation below about 0.15 (the iteration 1 failure pattern with low jitter), raise kp from 1.4 to about 1.6 and keep kd at 0.4, since kp 1.2 gave max_error of about 0.064 m with about one line-loss event per run.

If steering_oscillation stays above 0.15 (iteration 1 measured about 0.21) while the robot remains on the line, raise kd from 0.4 to about 0.5 or lower kp toward 1.2, to damp the turn command without giving up the steering gain.
If the oval finishes but completion_time rises above 3 s, raise base_speed from 1.0 toward 1.3, keeping kp and kd fixed, since base_speed 1.2 gave a mean oval time of 1.88 s.
